# Transportation Impact Brief: Maria (Concerned Elementary Parent)
**PERSONA-001 | FY27 Budget Analysis | Transportation**

---

## Executive Summary

The FY27 elementary consolidation proposals carry a transportation cost that the district has not fully quantified — and part of that cost lands directly on elementary families. Under Option A and Variant C, between **139 and 169 families** would have children split across two buildings, with no district-provided transport between them. The same configurations show a before/after care gap of up to **144 families**, at an estimated annual family cost of up to **$803,520** — a burden the budget documents do not acknowledge.

---

## Key Finding

**Option A's total fiscal exposure is $946,449–$1,679,845 per year — equal to 43% to 112% of the consolidation's claimed savings.**

That range is not a projection error. It reflects genuine uncertainty in how many families will need new care arrangements, what those arrangements will cost, and whether the district's 20 confirmed bus drivers can cover 30 required routes without additional hires. The district has not published an analysis that resolves this range.

---

## Configuration Comparison

| | **Option A** | **Option B** | **Variant C** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Split families** | 139–169 (18–24% of elementary) | 0 | 123–150 (16–21%) |
| **Care gap families** | 42–144 | 0 | 37–128 |
| **Family care cost (annual)** | $143,640–$803,520 | $0 | $126,540–$714,240 |
| **Bus tiers required** | 3–4 | 3 | 3–4 |
| **SEA driver shortfall** | −10 to −13 | −4 to −7 | −9 to −12 |
| **District cost (annual)** | $802,809–$876,325 | $30,365–$79,908 | $670,073–$735,597 |
| **Total fiscal exposure** | $946,449–$1,679,845 | $30,365–$79,908 | $796,613–$1,449,837 |
| **As % of claimed savings** | 43–112% | 1.4–5.3% | 36–97% |

**Note on the driver shortfall:** The 3/30/2026 Operations Director confirmed 20 drivers on staff. Option B — the lowest-impact configuration — still requires 24 routes. Every option has a driver gap. This was not modeled before the 14% SEA staffing cut was proposed.

**Note on before/after care:** After-care programs are currently **full at 4 of 5 elementary schools**. Only Kaler (the school proposed for closure) has openings. Families displaced into split-building schedules or shifted bell times have no guaranteed program to absorb them.

---

## What's Missing

The district has not published analysis on the following, despite direct questions at public sessions (TC-003, TC-006, TC-007, TC-009, TC-015):

1. **A route-level model** showing how 20–20 drivers cover 24–30 routes without overtime or new hires. The transportation consultant engagement was confirmed at the 3/30 meeting but described as "underway" — *after* the board vote, not before it.
2. **A 4th-tier cost estimate.** Option A and Variant C may require a 4th bus tier to handle grade-band routing. The driver idle window (9:30 AM–1:30 PM) leaves no margin for a 4th tier without overtime pay. No overtime cost estimate has been provided.
3. **A before/after care capacity audit** across all receiving schools. The district acknowledged the care concern at the March 2 forum but has not published waitlist data or expansion capacity for each program.
4. **A split-family transport alternative.** For the 139–169 families with children at two buildings under Option A, the district has not described whether any district-provided solution exists or whether families are expected to self-arrange.
5. **McKinney-Vento cost modeling by configuration.** Approximately 108 MV-eligible elementary students exist. Option A displaces the most students. Annual MV transport cost ranges from $54,337 to $127,853 under Option A, but the district has not published a configuration-specific MV cost estimate.

---

## Limitations

This analysis estimates family care costs using a per-child rate derived from current South Portland program pricing. Actual costs vary by provider and availability. The split-family count (139–169 under Option A) is modeled from enrollment data; the district has not confirmed or disputed this figure. The driver shortfall is computed against confirmed staffing of 20 drivers (3/30/2026); if additional hires occur before implementation, the gap narrows. All figures use FY25 as the budget baseline; the FY23 sensitivity run produces a slightly lower Option A exposure ($743K–$1.48M).

This analysis does not evaluate educational outcomes, consolidation rationale, or whether any configuration is the right policy choice.

---

## Invitation to Improve

This brief would be materially improved by the following district data:

- **Route model with driver assignments** — which routes are covered by which drivers, and what schedule changes are required under each configuration
- **Before/after care enrollment and waitlist data** for each elementary school, by grade
- **Confirmed bell schedule** under each configuration, including whether a 4th tier is required and its associated cost
- **McKinney-Vento student addresses by receiving school** — to compute displacement accurately per configuration
- **Transportation consultant scope and timeline** — specifically, when the route feasibility analysis will be complete and whether it will be published before the final budget vote

The district is encouraged to share any of this data publicly. It would allow this analysis to narrow its ranges and give families a clearer picture before decisions are final.

---

*Analysis based on SPEC-060 through SPEC-065. Configuration data reflects FY25 baseline. Driver staffing confirmed by Director of Operations Mike Natalie, 3/30/2026 budget workshop.*
